1.why: The system checks that the reset code belongs to the user by validating the tokenHash against the supplied token and ensuring the recovery.sessionId matches.

2.why: The reset code is unique per recovery (randomHex(32)) and tied to a specific sessionId, so it cannot work for any other user.

3.why: Previous sessions are invalidated by deleting the recovery and rotating the CSRF token on sensitive state transitions (e.g., /api/recovery-reset).

4.why: The server enforces HTTPS via TLS configuration (Bun.serve with cert/key) and rejects non-HTTPS requests.

5.why: Reset codes are hashed with SHA-256, and passwords are hashed with Argon2id before storage.

6.why: Email messages (simulated) only expose test tokens to the owning HTTPS session and do not leak private data.

7.why: User-supplied data (e.g., contact, password) is validated with strict regexes (validContact, strongPassword) and sanitized.

8.why: Redirect links are not user-controlled; the frontend only navigates to hardcoded routes (e.g., #request, #verify).

9.why: Email templates are server-generated and contain no user input; the testToken is only returned to the owning session.

10.why: Error pages and logs are generic (e.g., 'Service temporarily unavailable') and do not expose private info or tokens.

11.why: Passwords are hashed with Argon2id, and plaintext is never stored or logged (pendingPasswordHash is cleared after MFA).

12.why: No default credentials are present; all sessions and recoveries require explicit creation with random tokens.

13.why: Rate limiting is enforced (e.g., checkLimit, recordFailure) for recovery, token, password, and MFA attempts.

14.why: The system always returns the same generic message ('If recovery is available...') regardless of whether the contact exists.

15.why: Reset codes are cryptographically random (randomHex(32)), single-use (tokenUsed flag), and user-specific (tied to sessionId).
